Source: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

Abstract: This study operationalizes the organizing vision (OV) within the technology intelligence process to support a mindful adoption of IT innovations. Grounded in OV theory and technology intelligence research, this study adopts the echeloned Design Science Research (eDSR) methodology. An initial iteration across the first three echelons of the eDSR was conducted through a conceptual review of 35 OV definitions. This review identified the OV content, encompassing know-what, know-why, know-how, know-when, and know-where, as the central core component of the OV concept. The resulting initial framework offers a structured approach to transforming fragmented community discourse (containing the OV) into actionable intelligence. item.title: Green GenAI or, Dirty Infrastructure: Employees’ Perceived Ecological Impact Transparency of LLMs at Work
item.description:
Authors: Lutfi Al Nahin

Source: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution; Canada-related term in abstract: pei

Abstract: Generative AI systems are increasingly embedded in knowledge work, yet their environmental consequences remain largely invisible at the point of interaction (Watson et al., 2010; Verdecchia et al., 2023), while productivity benefits are immediate and salient. This opacity creates a sustainability governance challenge: employees cannot factor environmental costs into usage decisions they cannot observe. We introduce two constructs to address this gap. item.title: Discursive Enactment: Exploring the Alignment Between Community and Institutional Discourses
item.description:
Authors: Harold Junior Nguegang Tewamba, Elora J Das

Source: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution; Canada-related term in abstract: canada

Abstract: This research project aims to explore the discursive enactment of organizations in response to generative artificial intelligence by analyzing the alignment between community and institutional discourses. Drawing on organizing vision theory and IT mindfulness, we expect to propose a typology of IT mindfulness profiles based on the semantic and temporal alignment between these discourses. The methodology aims to employ dynamic topic modeling (BERTopic) to analyze data from X (Twitter) and from the official websites of each U15 Canada university between 2022 and 2026.

Abstract: Private blockchain adoptions are prone to failure, yet blockchain governance research has focused primarily on ecosystem-level structures rather than the micro-governance practices through which project leaders build internal legitimacy. Using an ethnographic case study of a successful Canadian public-sector-led private blockchain initiative in critical minerals mining, this study examines how leadership practices shape adoption success when leaders do not begin with superior blockchain expertise or sectoral prestige. The findings show that human-oriented values, project stewardship, and actionable optimism help build coordination capacity, collective learning, and internal credibility. Abstract: Digital education is often promoted as a solution to educational inequities in rural, northern, and Indigenous communities in Canada and globally. item.title: Central Sleep Apnea: Pathophysiology, Diagnosis and Classification.
item.description:
Authors: Clodagh M. Ryan, T Douglas Bradley

Source: PubMed

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Central sleep apnea (CSA) is a heterogeneous and relatively rare sleep breathing disorder characterized by recurrent reductions in respiratory drive and airflow during sleep. Its complex and not fully understood pathophysiology reflects challenges in respiratory control mechanisms. CSA is associated with cardiovascular, neurologic, systemic, and genetic conditions, and remains a key area for further research, particularly in improving diagnosis and understanding mechanisms. This article outlines the definition, diagnostic approaches, classification, and provides an overview of the underlying pathophysiology of CSA.
